There may be empty squares between these two stones, but no intervening stones To win, a player must place their stone, with no means of the opponent placing one, or place 5 adjacent tokens in any direction. [Rating: 5/10] I'm not sure whether or not this is a clever rendition on the connect-N formula. The catch here is that you must follow horizontally or vertically from your opponent's last play. This does seem to solve some of the more tempo-based issues and predictable chains of more classic connect-N games. Notably you pretty much must go for diagonal wins. I just can't tell if that is more interesting or not than orthogonal ones. Not bad, just less thrilling than Pente or Connect6
